reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right family (no capital, an unknown close rate that only selling measures), and the arithmetic is right: net per sale $500 - ($14.50 + $0.30) = $485.20, 3 sales = $1,455.60 < $1,500, so 4 sales ($1,940.80) are needed; Stripe's first payout 7-14 days after the first live payment puts order 1 (day 6) at day 20 at worst and later payouts inside the window. But the test is mis-specified in ways that matter before the owner acts on it. (1) validation.decides names only CONVERSION and CURRENT_DEMAND, yet every link of this opening is unestablished (Brain: CURRENT_DEMAND, OFFER_AND_PRICE, CONVERSION, FULFILMENT, ECONOMICS, SETTLES_IN_TIME). The $500 price has no evidence: the GoDaddy $640+ row is a guide figure of what a web designer charges, not what these buyers pay, and the verifier gate rejected it twice; the only thing that establishes the price is a buyer paying $500, so OFFER_AND_PRICE must be among what the test decides, and the 'undercuts a $640 floor' argument should be dropped as support. (2) The test takes $500 paid orders before fulfilment is shown possible: the fulfiller is 'the owner, drafting with AI tools' (a RECOMMENDATION fact), with no site yet built in 72 hours. Build and publish one sample 5-page site (or the mock previews) before the first charge, and add FULFILMENT to decides with a stop if a paid site cannot be delivered in 72 hours. (3) Owner hours are treated as available: the steps need about 24.5 owner hours (10 sending, 1 offer, 1 test, 4 closing, 8 building, 0.5 collecting) and the goal states none; mark owner hours UNKNOWN and make the owner's confirmation of ~25 hours over 3 weeks a start condition. (4) The buyer-volume quantity (6.15M = 17% x 36.2M) rests on claims the gate rejected (population mismatch; the 17% is a survey share of unstated sample) and should be UNKNOWN; the 200-business Google Maps list in s1 is the real count to state.
